        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Contributing to Meshery Server</h1>
           <p>As a new contributor, you’re going to want to familiarize with the project in order to resolve the issues in the best way. Installing and playing around with Meshery will give you context for any issues that you might work on.</p>

<p>Once an issue has been addressed, you’ll need to test it as well. Ideally, these tests are run from the user’s perspective (someone running Meshery in a container), not from a contributor’s perspective (someone running Meshery as a locally-compiled service).</p>

<h2 id="compiling-and-running-meshery-server">Compiling and Running Meshery server</h2>

<p>To build and run Meshery server from source:</p>

<ol>
  <li>First, build the static assets for the UI by running</li>
</ol>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">make ui-setup
make ui-build</code>
</div>
</pre>

<ol>
  <li>Next, build &amp; run the server code by running</li>
</ol>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">make server</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>Any time changes are made to the Go code, you will have to stop the server and run the above command again.
Once the Meshery server is up and running, you should be able to access Meshery on your <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">localhost</code> on port <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">9081</code> at <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">http://localhost:9081</code>. One thing to note, you might NOT see the <a href="#contributing-ui">Meshery UI</a> until the UI code is built as well.
After running Meshery server, you will need to select your <strong>Cloud Provider</strong> by navigating to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">localhost:9081</code>. Only then you will be able to use the Meshery UI on port <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">3000</code>.</p>

<p><strong>Please note</strong>: If you get error while starting the server as <strong>“Meshery Development Incompatible”</strong> then follow the below guideline 👇</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/meshery-development-incompatible-error.png">
  <img style="max-width: 450px;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/meshery-development-incompatible-error.png" />
</a></p>

<p>Potential Solution:</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p>Go to your meshery folder in your local-system where you’ve cloned it.
Execute:</p>
  </li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">git remote add upstream https://github.com/meshery/meshery</code></li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">git fetch upstream</code></li>
  <li>Restart the meshery server</li>
  <li>Additionally, before restarting the server, if you like to pull the latest changes, you can do: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">git pull upstream master</code></li>
</ul>

<h4 id="building-docker-image">Building Docker image</h4>

<p>To build a Docker image of Meshery, please ensure you have <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Docker</code> installed to be able to build the image. Now, run the following command to build the Docker image:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">make docker</code>
</div>
</pre>

<h4 id="define-and-validate-errors">Define and validate errors</h4>

<p>Every Golang-based component within the Meshery ecosystem incorporates a utility to define and manage error messages for every error instance. This is internally done with several make commands, but one can explicitly validate with the help of the following make command. This checks and validates the errors that are present in the particular project.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">make error</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>For more details, <a href="/v0.8/project/contributing/contributing-error">Error Utility</a></p>

<h3 id="configuring-log-levels-at-runtime">Configuring Log levels at Runtime</h3>

<p>The server log levels can be configured at runtime by changing the env variable <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">LOG_LEVEL</code> defined in file <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/server/cmd/server-config.env"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">server-config.env</code></a>. The configuration library (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">viper</code>) watches for the env file, any change in the file content results in the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">file_system</code> event to be emitted and the log level is updated accordingly.</p>

<p><strong><em>Should there be any alterations to the location or name of the environment file, it will result in the inability to configure log levels during runtime. In the event of such modifications, it is essential to update the server to preserve proper functionality.</em></strong></p>

<p>```Available Meshery Server log levels are:</p>
<ul>
  <li>Panic - 0</li>
  <li>Fatal - 1</li>
  <li>Error - 2</li>
  <li>Warn  - 3</li>
  <li>Info  - 4</li>
  <li>Debug - 5</li>
  <li>Trace level - 6
```</li>
</ul>

<p>The default setting for the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">LOG_LEVEL</code> is <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">4</code> (Info). However, if the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">DEBUG</code> environmental variable is configured as <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">TRUE</code>, it supersedes the value set in the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">LOG_LEVEL</code> environmental variable, and the logging level is then adjusted to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">5</code>(Debug).</p>

<h3 id="runtime-configuration-environment-variables">Runtime Configuration Environment Variables</h3>

<p>Meshery Server supports several runtime configuration environment variables that control various aspects of server behavior:</p>

<h4 id="provider-and-extension-configuration">Provider and Extension Configuration</h4>

<ul>
  <li><strong><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">PROVIDER_CAPABILITIES_FILEPATH</code></strong>: Specifies a local file path to load provider capabilities from a static JSON file instead of fetching from the remote provider’s endpoint. Useful for offline development and testing.
    <ul>
      <li>Default: Not set (capabilities fetched from remote provider)</li>
      <li>Example: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">PROVIDER_CAPABILITIES_FILEPATH=/path/to/capabilities.json</code></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">SKIP_DOWNLOAD_EXTENSIONS</code></strong>: Controls whether Meshery downloads and refreshes provider extension packages during login and capability refresh operations.
    <ul>
      <li>Default: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">false</code> (extensions are downloaded/refreshed)</li>
      <li>Example: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">SKIP_DOWNLOAD_EXTENSIONS=true</code></li>
      <li>Use cases: Development environments, pre-packaged deployments, reducing startup time</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<h4 id="kubernetes-configuration">Kubernetes Configuration</h4>

<ul>
  <li><strong><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">KUBECONFIG_FOLDER</code></strong>: Specifies the folder path where Meshery should look for Kubernetes configuration files. This allows you to provide a Meshery deployment with a predefined Kubernetes context.
    <ul>
      <li>Default: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">$HOME/.kube</code> (or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/home/appuser/.kube</code> in containerized deployments)</li>
      <li>Example: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">KUBECONFIG_FOLDER=/home/appuser/.kube</code></li>
      <li>Use cases: Custom kubeconfig locations, pre-configured Kubernetes contexts, containerized deployments</li>
      <li>Note: Meshery looks for a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">config</code> file within this folder (e.g., <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/home/appuser/.kube/config</code>)</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<h4 id="other-configuration-variables">Other Configuration Variables</h4>

<ul>
  <li><strong><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">SKIP_DOWNLOAD_CONTENT</code></strong>: Skips downloading seed content for patterns, filters, and applications.
    <ul>
      <li>Default: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">false</code></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">SKIP_COMP_GEN</code></strong>: Skips component generation during startup.
    <ul>
      <li>Default: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">false</code></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">PLAYGROUND</code></strong>: Enables playground mode for Meshery.
    <ul>
      <li>Default: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">false</code></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<h3 id="using-custom-meshkit-code-for-meshery-server-development">Using custom Meshkit code for Meshery server development</h3>

<ol>
  <li>
    <p>Checkout <strong>meshery</strong> and <strong>meshkit</strong> repository in adjacent directories.</p>
    
    <pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">
$ git clone https://github.com/meshery/meshery.git
$ git clone https://github.com/meshery/meshkit.git
    </code>
</div>
</pre>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p>In your <code>meshery</code> go.mod, update the meshkit package.</p>
    
    <pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">
github.com/meshery/meshkit =&gt; ../meshkit
    </code>
</div>
</pre>
    <p>Remember to remove this go.mod change when creating pull requests.</p>
  </li>
</ol>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

          <h1>Contributing to Meshery UI - Notification Center</h1>
           <div class="prereqs"><p><strong style="font-size: 20px;">Prerequisite Reading</strong></p>
  <ol><li><a href="contributing-ui">Contributing to Meshery UI</a></li></ol>
</div>

<h2 id="table-of-contents">Table of Contents</h2>

<ul>
  <li><a href="#what-is-the-notification-center">What is the Notification Center?</a></li>
  <li><a href="#metadata-formatter">Metadata Formatter</a></li>
  <li><a href="#how-notification-metadata-is-rendered">How Notification Metadata is Rendered</a></li>
  <li><a href="#types-of-event-specific-notification-formatters">Types of Event Specific Notification Formatters</a>
    <ul>
      <li><a href="#common-formatter">Common Formatter</a></li>
      <li><a href="#error-formatter">Error Formatter</a></li>
      <li><a href="#model-registration-formatter">Model Registration Formatter</a></li>
      <li><a href="#relationship-evaluation-formatter">Relationship Evaluation Formatter</a></li>
      <li><a href="#dry-run-formatter">Dry Run Formatter</a></li>
      <li><a href="#deployment-summary-formatter">Deployment Summary Formatter</a></li>
      <li><a href="#propertyformatters-and-propertylinkformatters">PropertyFormatters and PropertyLinkFormatters</a></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<video style="width:min(100%,750px)" height="auto" autoplay="" muted="" loop="">
  <source src="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/assets/65964225/345672de-3f61-4be0-b3c8-0e7480cc496c" type="video/mp4" />

<h2 id="what-is-the-notification-center">What is the Notification Center?</h2>

<p>The Notification Center is a dedicated panel in Meshery’s UI that helps you monitor, understand, and respond to events across your system. It acts as a central place where you can see important updates related to your infrastructure, workloads, and Meshery’s internal operations.</p>

<blockquote>
  <p>Want to understand how users interact with the Notification Center? <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/guides/infrastructure-management/notification-management">Learn more here</a>.</p>
</blockquote>

<hr />

<p>The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">NotificationCenter</code> component of Meshery UI Switching to Graphql subscriptions and implementing robust filtering. Events are persisted in Meshery Server and state management on client is done using Redux Toolkit and RTK.</p>

<h3 id="user-facing-features">User-facing Features</h3>

<ul>
  <li>Robust filtering support inspired by GitHub’s notification filtering style.
    <ul>
      <li>Search is also included.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>Proper hierarchial presentation of error details, including probable cause and suggested remeditation.</li>
  <li>Support for notification status (notifications can be marked as read and unread)
    <ul>
      <li><em>Future: Notifications can be acknowledged or resolved.</em></li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>Event-based notification via Graphql subscription (provided by Meshery Server and any upstream components or externally managed systems, like Kubernetes)</li>
  <li>Infinite scroll for pagination.</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="state-management-and-internal-details">State Management and Internal Details</h3>

<ul>
  <li>The State on client is managed using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Redux Tooltik</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Rtk-query</code></li>
  <li>Update and Delete operations are optimistically handled.</li>
  <li>Network Request are cached and are invalidated when new events come or events are deleted/updated.</li>
  <li>Due to need for infinite scroll and optimistic update the events are stored globally in Redux.</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="bulk-operations">Bulk Operations</h3>

<p>Bulk operations in the Notification Center allow users to perform actions like deleting multiple notifications or changing the status of multiple notifications in a batch. This documentation outlines the key features and functionality of bulk operations, including the restriction of performing only one bulk operation at a time, the disabling of buttons during ongoing operations, and the display of a loading icon to indicate ongoing activity.</p>

<h3 id="initiating-a-bulk-operation">Initiating a Bulk Operation</h3>

<ul>
  <li>Users select the notifications they want to include in the bulk operation. This is typically done by checking checkboxes next to each notification.</li>
  <li>After selecting notifications, users trigger the desired bulk operation (e.g., delete or change status) by clicking the corresponding action button.</li>
  <li>Once initiated, the bulk operation begins processing the selected notifications.</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="metadata-formatter">Metadata Formatter</h2>

<p>When the server sends an event, it follows a consistent schema that contains metadata intended for user presentation. This metadata typically includes fields such as <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">description</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">date</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">user_id</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">system_id</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">action</code>, and the resources involved.</p>

<p>In some cases, the metadata may also contain more detailed information—such as a traceback, a summary, or a complete error log—which is dynamically generated at runtime and encapsulated within the event.</p>

<p>Presenting this structured information in a clear and accessible way is essential, as it provides valuable insights into system behavior and ongoing operations.</p>

<p>To accomplish this task, we employ metadata formatters that transform structured data into visually appealing formats. There are currently two types of formatters in use:</p>

<ol>
  <li><strong>Metadata Specific Formatters:</strong> These formatters are specifically designed for particular types of metadata, such as Error and DryRunResponse. Metadata Specific Formatters are implemented as React components that take the metadata as input and render it within the component.</li>
  <li><strong>Dynamic Formatter:</strong> Since metadata can vary significantly in structure, it is not practical to create a specific formatter for each kind. Dynamic formatters analyze the schema’s structure and apply custom-defined rules for formatting:
    <ul>
      <li>Text strings are rendered using the BodySectionRenderer (more on this later).</li>
      <li>Arrays are rendered using the ArrayRenderer.</li>
      <li>Key-value pairs are rendered using the KeyValueRenderer.</li>
      <li>Nested objects are recursively rendered.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ol>

<h3 id="bodysectionrenderer">BodySectionRenderer</h3>

<p>The BodySectionRenderer is responsible for formatting and rendering raw text strings into React components. During this process, it parses the string to replace external links with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">&lt;Link&gt;</code> components and checks if the link matches predefined sites to render the link accordingly.</p>

<h3 id="arrayrenderer">ArrayRenderer</h3>

<p>The ArrayRenderer is responsible for rendering an array of items in a recursive manner, presenting them as a bulletized list using the MetdataFormatter.</p>

<h3 id="keyvaluerenderer">KeyValueRenderer</h3>

<p>Object properties with string values are considered key-value pairs and are rendered as such.</p>

<h3 id="the-metadata-specific-formatter">The Metadata Specific Formatter</h3>

<p>Certain metadata, such as Kubernetes responses and Errors, hold high importance and have dedicated renderers. These dedicated renderers can still utilize the dynamic formatter to format specific parts of the response, such as DryRunResponse.</p>

<h3 id="reusability">Reusability</h3>

<p>While this system was initially developed for our events and notification center, the components it comprises are highly reusable and can be employed in other contexts where dynamic formatting of structured data is required.</p>

<h2 id="how-notification-metadata-is-rendered">How Notification Metadata is Rendered</h2>

<p>When a notification event is received from the server, it includes a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">metadata</code> field containing structured, event-specific information. The purpose of formatters is to present this data in a clean, readable, and user-friendly format inside the expanded view of each notification.</p>

<p>The core logic for rendering metadata is handled by the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">FormattedMetadata</code> component in <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">metadata.js</code>, which follows this decision tree:</p>

<ol>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Event-Specific Formatter Check</strong><br />
If a formatter exists for the event’s type (registered under <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">EventTypeFormatters</code>), that dedicated formatter is used to fully control how the metadata is displayed.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Fallback to Property-Based Formatting</strong><br />
If no event-specific formatter is found, the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">FormattedMetadata</code> component falls back to the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">FormatStructuredData</code> function (also in <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">metadata.js</code>).</p>

    <ul>
      <li>This function renders each key-value pair from the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">metadata</code> using the mappings defined in:
        <ul>
          <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">PropertyFormatters</code> – for structured or specialized visual formats.</li>
          <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">PropertyLinkFormatters</code> – for rendering clickable links (e.g., file paths, URLs).</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ol>

<h3 id="key-files-and-directories">Key Files and Directories</h3>

<p>This section outlines the essential files and folders that you’ll interact with when working on Notification Center metadata formatters.</p>

<h4 id="notificationcenter-root-directory"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">NotificationCenter/</code> <em>(Root Directory)</em></h4>

<ul>
  <li><strong>index.js</strong>: Contains the main context provider (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">NotificationCenterProvider</code>), the drawer component (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">NotificationCenterDrawer</code>), and orchestrates the overall structure.</li>
  <li><strong>metadata.js</strong>: Defines <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">PropertyFormatters</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">LinkFormatters</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">PropertyLinkFormatters</code>, and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">EventTypeFormatters</code>. Contains the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">FormattedMetadata</code> component which decides <em>how</em> to format the metadata based on event type or specific properties.</li>
  <li><strong>notification.js</strong>: Defines how an individual notification is rendered.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="formatters-notificationcenterformatters"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">formatters/</code> <em>(NotificationCenter/formatters)</em></h4>

<p>This directory houses reusable formatter components dedicated to specific types of metadata or event types.</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>common.js</strong>: Contains shared components like <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">TitleLink</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">DataToFileLink</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">EmptyState</code>.</li>
  <li><strong>error.js</strong>: Defines <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ErrorMetadataFormatter</code> for displaying structured error details.</li>
  <li><strong>model_registration.js</strong>: Contains formatters for model import/registration events (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ModelImportMessages</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ModelImportedSection</code>).</li>
  <li><strong>pattern_dryrun.js</strong>: Defines <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">DryRunResponseFormatter</code> which utilizes components from <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">DesignLifeCycle</code>.</li>
  <li><strong>relationship_evaluation.js</strong>: Defines <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">RelationshipEvaluationEventFormatter</code> responsible for rendering notifications related to the evaluation of relationships between components in a design.</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="types-of-event-specific-notification-formatters">Types of Event Specific Notification Formatters</h2>

<h3 id="common-formatter">Common Formatter</h3>

<p>The following reusable components standardize how notification links, empty states, and downloadable traces are displayed:</p>

<ol>
  <li>
    <p><strong>TitleLink</strong>: Renders a styled title with an external link icon.<br />
Props:</p>

    <ul>
      <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">href</code> (required): URL of the link.</li>
      <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">children</code>: The link text.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><strong>EmptyState</strong>: Displays a description when no specific data is available for an event.<br />
Props:</p>

    <ul>
      <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">event.description</code> (optional): Text description of the event.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><strong>DataToFileLink</strong>: Converts event data into a downloadable <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.txt</code> file.<br />
Props:</p>
    <ul>
      <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">data</code> (required): Can be a string or JSON object.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ol>

<h3 id="error-formatter">Error Formatter</h3>

<p>The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ErrorMetadataFormatter</code> is used for formatting error-related notifications in the Meshery UI Notification Center. It structures error details, probable causes, and suggested remediations in a readable format.</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Details</strong>: A comprehensive explanation of the error, often broken into multiple points or steps.</li>
  <li><strong>Probable Cause</strong>: A list of potential reasons why the error occurred, helping the user understand the root cause.</li>
  <li><strong>Suggested Remediation</strong>: Actionable steps or recommendations to resolve the issue.</li>
  <li>Inside the ellipse menu, the user can find the error code docs link for further explanation of the error.</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Props:</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">metadata</code> (object): Contains error metadata fields such as:
    <ul>
      <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">LongDescription</code>: Provides details about the error.</li>
      <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ProbableCause</code>: Lists possible reasons for the error.</li>
      <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">SuggestedRemediation</code>: Suggests solutions to fix the error.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">event</code> (object, optional): Contains the notification event data.</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Path:</strong> <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ui/components/NotificationCenter/formatters/error.js</code></p>

<p><strong>Example:</strong></p>

<div class="language-javascript highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nx">ErrorMetadataFormatter</span>
  <span class="nx">metadata</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="na">LongDescription</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="dl">"</span><span class="s2">An unexpected error occurred while deploying the mesh.</span><span class="dl">"</span><span class="p">,</span>
    <span class="na">ProbableCause</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="dl">"</span><span class="s2">Misconfigured Kubernetes cluster.</span><span class="dl">"</span><span class="p">,</span>
    <span class="na">SuggestedRemediation</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="dl">"</span><span class="s2">Check your kubeconfig file and retry deployment.</span><span class="dl">"</span><span class="p">,</span>
  <span class="p">}</span>
  <span class="nx">event</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">{</span> <span class="na">description</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="dl">"</span><span class="s2">Mesh deployment failed</span><span class="dl">"</span> <span class="p">}</span>
<span class="sr">/</span><span class="err">&gt;
</span></code></pre></div></div>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/notification-center/error-formatter.png"><img alt="Error Formatter" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/notification-center/error-formatter.png" /></a></p>

<p><strong>When to Use:</strong></p>

<p>The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ErrorMetadataFormatter</code> is used when dealing with structured error events that follow a pattern (description, cause, remediation). A new formatter should be created only if the error metadata deviates significantly from the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ErrorMetadataFormatter</code> metadata structure.</p>

<h3 id="model-registration-formatter">Model Registration Formatter</h3>

<p>The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Model Registration Formatter</code> formats and displays model registration details, including components and relationships, in Meshery UI’s Notification Center. It ensures structured representation of imported models and error handling during the import process.</p>

<p><strong>Path:</strong> <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ui/components/NotificationCenter/formatters/model_registration.js</code></p>

<p><strong>Components:</strong></p>

<ol>
  <li>
    <p><strong>UnsuccessfulEntityWithError</strong>: This component is used to handle error cases during model import. It identifies the type and count of entities that failed to import.</p>

    <p><strong>Props:</strong></p>

    <ul>
      <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">modelName</code> (string): The name of the model being imported.</li>
      <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">error</code> (object): Contains details about the error encountered during import.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><strong>ModelImportedSection</strong>: Displays the details of the imported model along with components, relationships, and any errors that occur.</p>

    <p><strong>Props:</strong></p>

    <ul>
      <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">modelDetails</code> (object) – Contains model import data.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ol>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/notification-center/model-register-formatter.png"><img alt="Model Register Formatter" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/notification-center/model-register-formatter.png" /></a></p>

<h3 id="relationship-evaluation-formatter">Relationship Evaluation Formatter</h3>

<p>The <strong>Relationship Evaluation Formatter</strong> is responsible for rendering notifications related to the evaluation of relationships between components in a design. It provides a detailed breakdown of changes in components and relationships, such as additions, updates, and removals, during the evaluation process.</p>

<p><strong>Path:</strong> <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ui/components/NotificationCenter/formatters/relationship_evaluation.js</code></p>

<h4 id="key-components">Key Components</h4>

<ol>
  <li><strong>RelationshipEvaluationEventFormatter</strong>:<br />
The main formatter component that renders the event description and invokes the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">RelationshipEvaluationTraceFormatter</code> to display detailed traces.</li>
</ol>

<p><strong>Props:</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">event</code> (object): Contains:
    <ul>
      <li><strong>description</strong>: A description of the evaluation process.</li>
      <li><strong>metadata.trace</strong>: Contains categorized changes in components and relationships:
        <ul>
          <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">componentsAdded</code> (Array)</li>
          <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">componentsUpdated</code> (Array)</li>
          <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">componentsRemoved</code> (Array)</li>
          <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">relationshipsAdded</code> (Array)</li>
          <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">relationshipsUpdated</code> (Array)</li>
          <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">relationshipsRemoved</code> (Array)</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/notification-center/relationship-evaluation-formatter.png"><img alt="Relationship Evaluation Formatter" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/notification-center/relationship-evaluation-formatter.png" /></a></p>

<h4 id="when-to-use">When to Use</h4>

<p>The <strong>Relationship Evaluation Formatter</strong> is specifically designed to handle notifications related to changes in components and their relationships during an evaluation process. Use this formatter in the following scenarios:</p>

<ol>
  <li>When a notification involves the evaluation of relationships between components in a design.</li>
  <li>When you need to display categorized changes in components and relationships.</li>
  <li>When the event metadata includes a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">trace</code> object containing detailed information about the changes in components and relationships.</li>
</ol>

<h4 id="user-experience-relationship-evaluation-notification">User Experience: Relationship Evaluation Notification</h4>

<ol>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Evaluation Summary</strong>:<br />
The notification starts with a summary of the evaluation process.<br />
Example:<br />
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">"Relationship evaluation completed for design 'Deploy Meshery using Meshery-X' at version '0.0.11'"</code><br />
This gives the user context about which design and version were evaluated.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Detailed Changes</strong>:<br />
The notification breaks down the changes into categories:</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Components</strong>:
        <ul>
          <li><strong>Added</strong>: New components introduced in the design.</li>
          <li><strong>Updated</strong>: Existing components that were modified.</li>
          <li><strong>Removed</strong>: Components that were deleted from the design.</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
      <li><strong>Relationships</strong>:
        <ul>
          <li><strong>Added</strong>: New relationships established between components.</li>
          <li><strong>Updated</strong>: Existing relationships that were modified.</li>
          <li><strong>Removed</strong>: Relationships that were deleted.</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Component Details</strong>:<br />
For each component, the notification displays:</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Kind</strong>: The type of the component (e.g., <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Deployment</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Service</code>).</li>
      <li><strong>Name</strong>: The name of the component.</li>
      <li><strong>Model and Version</strong>: The model and version associated with the component.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Relationship Details</strong>:<br />
For each relationship, the notification displays:</p>
    <ul>
      <li><strong>Type</strong>: The type of relationship.</li>
      <li><strong>Source and Target</strong>: The components involved in the relationship (e.g., <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Pod</code> to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Pod</code>).</li>
      <li><strong>Model and Version</strong>: The model and version associated with the relationship.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ol>

<h3 id="dry-run-formatter">Dry Run Formatter</h3>

<p>The <strong>Dry Run Formatter</strong> is responsible for rendering notifications related to the dry run validation of a design. A dry run simulates the deployment or undeployment of a design to identify potential errors without actually applying the changes.</p>

<p><strong>Path:</strong> <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ui/components/DesignLifeCycle/DryRun.js</code></p>

<h4 id="key-components-1">Key Components</h4>

<ol>
  <li><strong>FormatDryRunResponse</strong>:<br />
The main formatter component that renders the dry run validation results. It displays the total number of errors.</li>
</ol>

<p><strong>Props:</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>dryRunErrors</strong> (array): An array of errors detected during the dry run. Each error includes:
    <ul>
      <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">type</code>: The type of error (e.g., <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">RequestError</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ComponentError</code>).</li>
      <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">fieldPath</code>: The specific field in the design where the error occurred.</li>
      <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">message</code>: A detailed error message.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li><strong>configurableComponentsCount</strong> (number): The number of configurable components in the design.</li>
  <li><strong>annotationComponentsCount</strong> (number): The number of annotation components in the design.</li>
  <li><strong>validationMachine</strong> (object): The state machine handling the dry run validation process.</li>
  <li><strong>currentComponentName</strong> (string): The name of the component currently being validated.</li>
</ul>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/notification-center/dry-run-formatter.png"><img alt="Dry Run Formatter" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/assets/img/notification-center/dry-run-formatter.png" /></a></p>

<h4 id="when-to-use-1">When to Use</h4>

<p>The <strong>Dry Run Formatter</strong> is used in the following scenarios:</p>

<ol>
  <li>When a notification involves the validation of a design through a dry run process.</li>
  <li>When you need to display errors detected during the dry run.</li>
  <li>When the event metadata includes details about configurable and annotation components.</li>
</ol>

<h2 id="deployment-summary-formatter">Deployment Summary Formatter</h2>

<p>The <strong>Deployment Summary Formatter</strong> is responsible for rendering notifications related to the deployment or undeployment of components in a design.</p>

<p><strong>Path:</strong> <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ui/components/DesignLifeCycle/DeploymentSummary.js</code></p>

<h4 id="key-components-2">Key Components</h4>

<ol>
  <li><strong>DeploymentSummaryFormatter</strong>:<br />
This component is used to display:
    <ul>
      <li><strong>Event Description</strong>: A brief description of the deployment event.</li>
      <li><strong>Errors</strong>: Any errors encountered during the deployment process.</li>
      <li><strong>Component Details</strong>: A list of components with their deployment status and metadata.</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ol>

<p><strong>Props:</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>event</strong> (object): Contains:
    <ul>
      <li><strong>description</strong>: A brief description of the deployment event.</li>
      <li><strong>action</strong>: The type of action performed (e.g., <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">deploy</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">undeploy</code>).</li>
      <li><strong>severity</strong>: The severity level of the event.</li>
      <li><strong>metadata</strong>:
        <ul>
          <li><strong>summary</strong>: A detailed summary of the deployment process, including component details.</li>
          <li><strong>error</strong>: Any errors encountered during the deployment process.</li>
          <li><strong>design_name</strong>: The name of the design being deployed.</li>
          <li><strong>design_id</strong>: The ID of the design being deployed.</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<h4 id="when-to-use-2">When to Use</h4>

<p>The <strong>Deployment Summary Formatter</strong> should be used in the following scenarios:</p>

<ol>
  <li><strong>Deployment or Undeployment Events</strong>:<br />
When the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">event.action</code> is either <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">deploy</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">undeploy</code> and the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">event.metadata</code> includes <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">design_name</code>.</li>
  <li>When a notification involves the deployment or undeployment of a design.</li>
</ol>

<h3 id="propertyformatters-and-propertylinkformatters">PropertyFormatters and PropertyLinkFormatters</h3>

<p><strong>Purpose:</strong><br />
When an event does not match an event in <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">EventTypeFormatters</code>, <strong>PropertyFormatters</strong> and <strong>PropertyLinkFormatters</strong> are used to format and render specific metadata fields in a structured and visually appealing way.</p>

<h4 id="examples-of-property-formatters">Examples of Property Formatters</h4>

<ol>
  <li><strong>trace</strong>: Converts large trace data into a downloadable file link.</li>
  <li><strong>ShortDescription</strong>: Displays a short description of the event.</li>
  <li><strong>Error</strong>: Uses the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ErrorMetadataFormatter</code> to display structured error details.</li>
</ol>

<h4 id="when-to-use-3">When to Use</h4>

<p>Use <strong>PropertyFormatters</strong> and <strong>PropertyLinkFormatters</strong> in the following scenarios:</p>

<ol>
  <li>When an event does not have a specific <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">EventTypeFormatter</code> defined.</li>
  <li>When you need to render individual metadata fields in a structured and visually appealing way.</li>
  <li>When metadata includes fields like trace data, short descriptions, or error details that require specialized formatting.</li>
</ol>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

<!-- <a href="http://idratherbewriting.com" class="noCrossRef productSubtitle"> Home </a> > <a class="noCrossRef productSubtitle" href="https://docs.meshery.io">Learn API Doc</a> > contributing-ui-schemas -->

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Schema-Driven UI Development in Meshery</h1>
           <p>Meshery aims to decouple the UI logic from hardcoded structures and become fully schema-driven. This allows the UI to dynamically adapt based on changes in the underlying schema without requiring constant manual updates. This document explains how to integrate schema definitions from the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/schemas"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">meshery/schemas</code></a> repository into the Meshery UI using a code-generation approach.</p>

<hr />

<h2 id="overview">Overview</h2>

<p>Meshery’s schemas define the <strong>structure of data (constructs)</strong> using JSON Schema and <strong>their behavior (API operations)</strong> using OpenAPI specifications. From these definitions, Meshery auto-generates:</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Go structs</strong> for backend validation and API handling</li>
  <li><strong>TypeScript types and objects</strong> for frontend development</li>
  <li><strong>Templates</strong> in JSON and YAML formats</li>
</ul>

<p>This approach ensures the <strong>schemas remain the single source of truth</strong>.</p>

<hr />

<h2 id="repository-structure">Repository Structure</h2>

<p>All schema definitions live in the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/schemas"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">meshery/schemas</code></a> repository.</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>schemas/
  constructs/
    v1beta1/
      design/
        design.json              # JSON schema for the noun
        design_template.json     # JSON template (generated)
        design_template.yaml     # YAML template (generated)
        openapi.yml               # OpenAPI spec defining operations
        subschemas/               # Optional reusable schema parts
</code></pre></div></div>

<ul>
  <li><strong><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">&lt;construct&gt;.json</code></strong>: Defines structure (noun) — e.g., what a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Design</code> looks like.</li>
  <li><strong><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">openapi.yml</code></strong>: Describes operations (verbs) — e.g., how to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">GET</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">POST</code>, or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">DELETE</code> a design.</li>
  <li><strong><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Templates</code></strong>: Valid, default-filled, resolved objects from the schema.</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="schema-driven-ui-development-workflow">Schema-Driven UI Development Workflow</h2>

<p>Meshery follows a <strong>schema-first</strong> approach where the UI is driven by JSON schemas and OpenAPI specifications. Here’s how you can contribute to and use these schemas in the Meshery UI.</p>

<hr />

<h3 id="step-1-define-or-update-the-schema">Step 1: Define or Update the Schema</h3>

<p>If you’re introducing or modifying a UI feature that requires a new schema:</p>

<ol>
  <li>
    <p>Navigate to the appropriate schema directory:</p>

    <div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>schemas/constructs/&lt;version&gt;/&lt;construct&gt;/
</code></pre></div>    </div>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p>Define the schema structure in <strong><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">&lt;construct&gt;.json</code></strong> using <strong>JSON Schema v7</strong>.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p>Define API operations related to this schema in <strong><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">openapi.yml</code></strong> using <strong>OpenAPI v3</strong>. This helps generate consistent API types and models that align with your UI needs.</p>
  </li>
</ol>

<hr />

<h3 id="step-2-generate-typescript-types-and-schema-objects">Step 2: Generate TypeScript Types and Schema Objects</h3>

<p>Use the following command to generate TypeScript types and JavaScript schema objects:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>make generate-types
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>This will:</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p>Generate <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.ts</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.d.ts</code> files under:</p>

    <div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>typescript/constructs/&lt;version&gt;/&lt;construct&gt;/
</code></pre></div>    </div>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p>Create:</p>

    <ul>
      <li><strong>Typed interfaces</strong> for schema validation and component props</li>
      <li><strong>Schema objects</strong> usable for dynamic UI (e.g., forms, validations)</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<hr />

<h3 id="step-3-build-and-export-typesschema-objects">Step 3: Build and Export Types/Schema Objects</h3>

<p>After generation:</p>

<ol>
  <li>
    <p>Open <a href="https://github.com/meshery/schemas/blob/master/typescript/index.ts"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">typescript/index.ts</code></a></p>

    <ul>
      <li>Export the newly generated types and schema objects from here.</li>
      <li>
        <p>Example:</p>

        <div class="language-ts highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">export</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="k">from</span> <span class="dl">"</span><span class="s2">./constructs/v1beta1/design</span><span class="dl">"</span><span class="p">;</span>
</code></pre></div>        </div>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p>Build the TypeScript package to make the changes usable:</p>

    <div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>npm run build
</code></pre></div>    </div>
  </li>
</ol>

<hr />

<h3 id="step-4-use-schema-package-in-ui">Step 4: Use Schema Package in UI</h3>

<p>To consume the schema in the UI:</p>

<ol>
  <li>
    <p>Install the schema package locally:</p>

    <div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>npm <span class="nb">install</span> &lt;path-to-schemas-repo&gt;
</code></pre></div>    </div>

    <p>Examples:</p>

    <ul>
      <li>
        <p>Relative path:</p>

        <div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>npm <span class="nb">install</span> ../../schemas
</code></pre></div>        </div>
      </li>
      <li>
        <p>Absolute path:</p>

        <div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>npm <span class="nb">install</span> /home/user/code/schemas
</code></pre></div>        </div>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p>This will update your <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">package.json</code> to something like:</p>

    <div class="language-json highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nl">"@meshery/schema"</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">"file:../../schemas"</span><span class="w">
</span></code></pre></div>    </div>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p>Now you can import types and schema objects in your UI components:</p>
  </li>
</ol>

<h4 id="example-importing-and-using-a-type">Example: Importing and Using a Type</h4>

<div class="language-ts highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">import</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nx">DesignTypes</span> <span class="p">}</span> <span class="k">from</span> <span class="dl">"</span><span class="s2">@meshery/schema</span><span class="dl">"</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="c1">// Type safety!</span>
<span class="kd">const</span> <span class="nx">renderDesignCard</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="nx">design</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nx">Design</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">=&gt;</span> <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nx">div</span><span class="o">&gt;</span><span class="p">{</span><span class="nx">design</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">name</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="sr">/div&gt;</span><span class="err">;
</span></code></pre></div></div>

<h4 id="example-accessing-runtime-schema">Example: Accessing Runtime Schema</h4>

<div class="language-ts highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">import</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nx">DesignSchema</span> <span class="p">}</span> <span class="k">from</span> <span class="dl">"</span><span class="s2">@meshery/schema</span><span class="dl">"</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="kd">const</span> <span class="nx">validateDesign</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="nx">data</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">=&gt;</span> <span class="p">{</span>
  <span class="kd">const</span> <span class="nx">isValid</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nx">ajv</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">validate</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nx">DesignSchema</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nx">data</span><span class="p">);</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="nx">isValid</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">};</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Can't find a Schema Import in the UI?</h4>

  <p>If you're trying to import a schema object or type in the UI but it's missing, it's likely because it hasn't been exported yet from the schemas package.</p>
  <p>To keep the package lightweight, only actively used types and objects are exported by default. If you need access to a new schema, simply export it in the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/schemas" target="_blank">Meshery Schemas repository</a> and regenerate the package.</p>

</div>

<hr />

<h2 id="integration-points-in-ui">Integration Points in UI</h2>

<h3 id="a-rjsf-json-schemas">A. RJSF JSON Schemas</h3>

<p>Meshery uses <a href="https://github.com/rjsf-team/react-jsonschema-form">react-jsonschema-form</a> to render forms dynamically based on JSON schemas. All of Meshery’s RJSF schemas are defined in the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@sistent/sistent</code> package, which extends schemas from the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@meshery/schema</code> package.</p>

<p>This approach enables us to generate forms that automatically adapt to the schema structure without hardcoding field properties like type, enum, description, and others.</p>

<div class="language-ts highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">import</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nx">DesignSchema</span> <span class="p">}</span> <span class="k">from</span> <span class="dl">"</span><span class="s2">@meshery/schema</span><span class="dl">"</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="kd">const</span> <span class="nx">designSchema</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">{</span>
  <span class="p">...</span><span class="nx">DesignSchema</span><span class="p">,</span>
  <span class="na">properties</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="p">...</span><span class="nx">DesignSchema</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">properties</span><span class="p">,</span>
    <span class="na">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">{</span>
      <span class="p">...</span><span class="nx">DesignSchema</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">properties</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">name</span><span class="p">,</span>
      <span class="na">description</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nx">DesignSchema</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">properties</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">description</span><span class="p">,</span>
      <span class="na">ui</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">{</span>
        <span class="na">label</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nx">DesignSchema</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">properties</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">name</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">title</span><span class="p">,</span>
        <span class="na">placeholder</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nx">DesignSchema</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">properties</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">name</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">description</span><span class="p">,</span>
      <span class="p">},</span>
    <span class="p">},</span>
    <span class="c1">// Other properties with UI-specific enhancements</span>
  <span class="p">},</span>
<span class="p">};</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<hr />

<h3 id="b-general-form-ui">B. General Form UI</h3>

<p>OpenAPI schemas (especially request bodies for POST/PUT operations) serve as the foundation for building form logic. These definitions include:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Field validations (e.g. <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">required</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">format</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">maxLength</code>)</li>
  <li>Field types and formats (e.g. <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">string</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">integer</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">date-time</code>)</li>
  <li>Descriptions and examples</li>
  <li>Enum constraints and conditional logic</li>
  <li>Custom extensions like <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">x-rjsf-*</code> for layout</li>
</ul>

<p>This ensures alignment between frontend form behavior and backend expectations.</p>

<div class="language-ts highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">import</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nx">DesignTypes</span> <span class="p">}</span> <span class="k">from</span> <span class="dl">"</span><span class="s2">@meshery/schema</span><span class="dl">"</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="kd">const</span> <span class="nx">DesignForm</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">({</span> <span class="nx">design</span> <span class="p">}:</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nl">design</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nx">DesignTypes</span> <span class="p">})</span> <span class="o">=&gt;</span> <span class="p">(</span>
  <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nx">form</span><span class="o">&gt;</span>
    <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nx">input</span> <span class="kd">type</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="dl">"</span><span class="s2">text</span><span class="dl">"</span> <span class="nx">value</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">{</span><span class="nx">design</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">name</span><span class="p">}</span> <span class="sr">/</span><span class="err">&gt;
</span>    <span class="p">{</span><span class="cm">/* More fields derived from the schema */</span><span class="p">}</span>
  <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="sr">/form</span><span class="err">&gt;
</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<hr />

<h3 id="c-ui-specific-descriptions-and-enhancements">C. UI-Specific Descriptions and Enhancements</h3>

<p>Any UI-specific metadata—such as <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">name</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">type</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">hints</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">descriptions</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">defaults</code>, etc.—is defined directly within the relevant schema object. Elements like tooltips, descriptions, and other metadata are frequently needed across the UI, so having a single source of truth in the schema object ensures consistency and reduces duplication.</p>

<p>For example, if we have a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Design</code> schema, the UI retrieves details like the design’s name, description, and other properties directly from the schema object.</p>

<hr />

<h3 id="d-type-safety-for-component-props">D. Type Safety for Component Props</h3>

<p>Generated TypeScript types from the schema ensure UI components are type-safe and consistent with backend contracts.</p>

<div class="language-ts highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">import</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nx">DesignTypes</span> <span class="p">}</span> <span class="k">from</span> <span class="dl">"</span><span class="s2">@meshery/schema</span><span class="dl">"</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="kd">const</span> <span class="nx">DesignCard</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">({</span> <span class="nx">design</span> <span class="p">}:</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nl">design</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nx">DesignTypes</span> <span class="p">})</span> <span class="o">=&gt;</span> <span class="p">(</span>
  <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nx">div</span><span class="o">&gt;</span>
    <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nx">h2</span><span class="o">&gt;</span><span class="p">{</span><span class="nx">design</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">name</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="sr">/h2</span><span class="err">&gt;
</span>    <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nx">p</span><span class="o">&gt;</span><span class="p">{</span><span class="nx">design</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">description</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="sr">/p</span><span class="err">&gt;
</span>  <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="sr">/div</span><span class="err">&gt;
</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

          <h1>Contributing to Meshery UI - Sistent</h1>
           <div class="prereqs"><p><strong style="font-size: 20px;">Prerequisite Reading</strong></p>
  <ol><li><a href="contributing-ui">Contributing to Meshery UI</a></li></ol>
</div>

<h2 id="contributing-to-meshery-ui---sistent"><a name="contributing-ui-sistent">Contributing to Meshery UI - Sistent</a></h2>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Sistent</code> is the design system used by Meshery UI. Sistent is an open source design system that offers building blocks to create consistent, accessible, and user-friendly interfaces. It’s aimed at developers who want to design applications aligned with the same brand and ensure a uniform user experience across different products.</p>

<p>Sistent leverages Material UI libraries and provides a custom theme on top of it for a consistent look and feel. It includes components, icons, and design tokens that developers can readily integrate into their applications. By using Sistent, developers can save time and effort while maintaining a high-quality user experience throughout Meshery.</p>

<p><strong>Example</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li>This <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Modal</code> is a Sistent Standard Modal used in validation of design.</li>
</ul>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/sistent/sistent-modal.png">
<img style="width: 600px;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/sistent/sistent-modal.png" />
</a></p>

<h3 id="how-to-use-sistent-in-meshery-ui">How to use Sistent in Meshery UI</h3>

<p><strong>Table of Contents</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li><a href="#usage">Usage</a></li>
  <li><a href="#how-to-use-tokenscolors-from-sistent-theme">How to use Sistent tokens/theme colors</a></li>
  <li><a href="#examples">Examples</a></li>
</ul>

<p>The Sistent design system includes a variety of base components such as <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Button</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Textfield</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Checkbox</code>, and more, which can be found <a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sistent/sistent/tree/master/src/base">here</a>
Additionally, it provides custom components like <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Modal</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">TransferList</code>, and others, which are available <a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sistent/sistent">here</a></p>

<h3 id="usage">Usage</h3>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Import any base or custom component from <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@sistent/sistent</code></strong>. Here’s how you can do it:</li>
</ul>

<div class="language-javascript highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">import</span> <span class="p">{</span><span class="nx">Button</span><span class="p">}</span> <span class="k">from</span> <span class="s2">`@sistent/sistent`</span>

<span class="kd">function</span> <span class="nx">MyComponent</span><span class="p">()</span> <span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="p">(</span>
    <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nx">div</span><span class="o">&gt;</span>
      <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nx">Button</span>
        <span class="nx">variant</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="dl">"</span><span class="s2">contained</span><span class="dl">"</span>
        <span class="nx">onClick</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">{</span><span class="nx">onClick</span><span class="p">}</span>
      <span class="o">&gt;</span>
      <span class="p">{</span><span class="cm">/* Text to display */</span><span class="p">}</span>
      <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="sr">/Button</span><span class="err">&gt;
</span>    <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="sr">/div</span><span class="err">&gt;
</span>  <span class="p">);</span>
<span class="p">}</span>

<span class="k">export</span> <span class="k">default</span> <span class="nx">MyComponent</span><span class="p">;</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h3 id="how-to-use-tokenscolors-from-sistent-theme">How to use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Tokens/Colors</code> from Sistent theme</h3>

<p>Let’s start with a few of the common terms that we will come across frequently, as understanding what they mean will inform us of applicable use cases and proper procedures that should not be overlooked.</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Theme:</strong>
A theme provides a cohesive and consistent look and feel for a product, achieved through harmonious color palettes, legible fonts, and layout patterns. Sistent specifies both light and dark themes.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Value:</strong>
A value is a unique visual attribute assigned to a token via themes, such as hex codes or RGBA values, used to highlight specific colors. Avoid referencing exact values directly to ensure consistency; instead, use tokens to manage and implement reusable values.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Tokens:</strong>
Tokens serve as a shared language between design and development, detailing how to build user interfaces. Tokens represent context (background, text, component), role (success, warning, brand, inverse), and modifiers (secondary, tertiary, hover) derived from the <a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sistent/sistent">color palette</a>.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Role:</strong>
Roles specify the context for applying colors. Different roles can share the same value but will have different use cases due to the token structure. These values can vary depending on the current theme.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<h4 id="how-to-use-these-tokenscolors-from-sistent-theme">How to use these tokens/colors from Sistent theme</h4>

<ul>
  <li>Import the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">useTheme</code> hook from <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@sistent/sistent</code> to access the current theme.</li>
  <li>Utilize the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">useTheme</code> hook to access theme properties and apply them to your components, such as setting the background style of the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Button</code>.</li>
</ul>

<div class="language-javascript highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">import</span> <span class="p">{</span><span class="nx">Button</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nx">useTheme</span><span class="p">}</span> <span class="k">from</span> <span class="dl">"</span><span class="s2">@sistent/sistent</span><span class="dl">"</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="kd">function</span> <span class="nx">MyComponent</span><span class="p">()</span> <span class="p">{</span>
  <span class="kd">const</span> <span class="nx">theme</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nx">useTheme</span><span class="p">();</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="p">(</span>
    <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nx">div</span><span class="o">&gt;</span>
      <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nx">Button</span>
        <span class="nx">variant</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="dl">"</span><span class="s2">contained</span><span class="dl">"</span>
        <span class="nx">onClick</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">{</span><span class="nx">onClick</span><span class="p">}</span>
        <span class="nx">style</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">{{</span>
          <span class="na">background</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nx">theme</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">palette</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">background</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="k">default</span><span class="p">,</span>
          <span class="na">text</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nx">theme</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">palette</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">text</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">secondary</span><span class="p">,</span>
        <span class="p">}}</span>
      <span class="o">&gt;</span>
        <span class="p">{</span><span class="cm">/* Text to display */</span><span class="p">}</span>
        <span class="nx">Click</span> <span class="nx">Me</span>
      <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="sr">/Button</span><span class="err">&gt;
</span>    <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="sr">/div</span><span class="err">&gt;
</span>  <span class="p">);</span>
<span class="p">}</span>

<span class="k">export</span> <span class="k">default</span> <span class="nx">MyComponent</span><span class="p">;</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">NOTE</h4>
The <a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sistent/sistent">tokens</a> and their roles are specific to their use. For example, use the background palette for background styles and the text palette for text styles.
</div>
