<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

<!-- <a href="http://idratherbewriting.com" class="noCrossRef productSubtitle"> Home </a> > <a class="noCrossRef productSubtitle" href="https://docs.meshery.io">Learn API Doc</a> > contributing-ui-tests -->

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Contributing to Meshery UI End-to-End Tests</h1>
           <p>To automate functional integration and end-to-end testing Meshery uses <a href="https://playwright.dev/">Playwright</a> as one of the tools to automate browser testing. End-to-end tests run with each pull request to ensure that the changes do not break the existing functionality.</p>

<h2 id="prerequisites">Prerequisites:</h2>

<p>Before diving into Meshery’s testing environment, certain prerequisites are necessary:</p>

<ul>
  <li>A verified account in your chosen provider which integrate with Meshery.</li>
  <li>A compatible browser such as Chromium, Chrome, or Firefox.</li>
  <li>Installations of Golang, NodeJS, and Makefiles for Native OS build (Optional for docker based build).</li>
  <li>Kubernetes clusters (Required for connection to Kubernetes test cases)</li>
  <li>Already have <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/concepts/architecture/adapters">Meshery Adapters</a> up and running (Required for adapters test cases)</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="setting-up-environment-variable">Setting up environment variable</h2>

<p>To run the tests successfully, three environment variables must be configured:<br />
• <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">REMOTE_PROVIDER_USER_EMAIL</code> (Required): The email associated with your account within your provider.<br />
• <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">REMOTE_PROVIDER_USER_PASSWORD</code> (Required): The password associated with your account within your provider.<br />
• <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">PROVIDER_TOKEN</code> (Optional): Your provider token, can be generated from an account registered within your provider</p>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Accessing Remote Providers</h4>
In the case you are using Meshery Cloud as a remote provider, you can <a href="https://cloud.meshery.io/security/tokens">generate a token from your user account</a> to use while writing and executing tests.
</div>

<p>During the setup phase, Playwright utilizes these environment variables to log in and store credentials securely in the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">playwright/.auth</code> directory. To protect sensitive data, the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.gitignore</code> file is configured to exclude the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.env</code> file and any JSON files within the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">/playwright/.auth</code> directory from the GitHub repository.</p>

<p>There are several tools to help you to working with environment variables locally for each project such as <a href="https://github.com/direnv/direnv">direnv</a>, it can work across multiple shell such as Bash, Powershell, Oh my zsh, Fish, etc</p>

<h2 id="starting-up-meshery-ui-and-server">Starting up Meshery UI and Server</h2>

<p>There are a few ways to set up the Meshery UI and server, but for end-to-end testing, we aim to get as close to a production environment as possible. We know developers might need to make some tweaks for UI and Server. Rebuilding the whole project can take time, and we don’t support hot reload because it’s more for development than for end-to-end testing.</p>

<div class="alert alert-warning">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Several Test may break</h4>
Some test cases required you to have kubernetes cluster and build meshery adapter as well, be aware of that. Which is out of scope for this documentation<ul><li><a href="https://docs.meshery.io/installation/kubernetes/minikube">Kubernetes Cluster</a>: Installation of kubernetes cluster with Minikube.</li>
<li><a href="https://docs.meshery.io/installation/multiple-adapters">Meshery Adapters</a>: Using Multiple Adapters</li></ul>
</div>

<h3 id="native-os-build-recommended">Native OS Build (Recommended)</h3>

<p>This approach is very quick to build, but also dependent on your operating system, so you need to have all dependencies necessary to be able compile and running the server.</p>

<ul>
  <li>Install &amp; Build the NextJS application for both the UI and UI Provider</li>
</ul>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>make ui-build
</code></pre></div></div>

<ul>
  <li>Compile the Golang into binary file for Meshery Server</li>
</ul>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>make build-server
</code></pre></div></div>

<ul>
  <li>Run the Meshery Server on localhost port 9081</li>
</ul>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>make server-binary
</code></pre></div></div>

<h3 id="meshery-cli">Meshery CLI</h3>

<p>There is also Meshery CLI which can help you run the UI and Server, for more detail, you go to <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/project/contributing/contributing-cli-guide#process">Meshery CLI documentation</a></p>

<h3 id="docker-based-build">Docker Based Build</h3>

<p>Alternatively, a Docker-based setup can be utilized, simplifying the process, and ensuring consistency across different environments. It is closer to the production environment than the native solution but slower in terms of build time.</p>

<ul>
  <li>Build the docker container locally:</li>
</ul>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>make docker-testing-env-build
</code></pre></div></div>

<ul>
  <li>Run the docker container on port 9081</li>
</ul>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>make docker-testing-env
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="setup-playwright">Setup Playwright</h2>

<p>For Playwrights, always try to use a native OS whenever possible. The Docker-based approach is intended only for unsupported OSes and is generally not recommended because it runs on top of Ubuntu images, which can be redundant if you already using Ubuntu or Windows.</p>

<h3 id="playwright-on-native-os-recommended">Playwright on Native OS (Recommended)</h3>

<p>Setup playwright:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>make ui-test-setup
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Run the all project and test cases:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>make ui-test
</code></pre></div></div>

<h3 id="playwright-server-on-docker-based-image">Playwright server on docker based image</h3>

<p>The first step is to pull the docker image from <a href="https://mcr.microsoft.com/en-us/product/playwright/tags">Azure Container Registry</a> where the playwright stores their image using this command:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>docker pull mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:&lt;version&gt;-&lt;base-image&gt;
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="alert alert-warning">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Playwright Versioning</h4>
Make sure the version you are using matches the version of `@playwright/test` in the `package.json` dev dependencies
</div>

<p>Here is the example of pulling playwright v1.44.0 with Ubuntu 22.04 LTS</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>docker pull mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.44.0-jammy
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Starting up playwright docker server:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>docker run <span class="nt">--rm</span> <span class="nt">--network</span> host <span class="nt">--init</span> <span class="nt">-it</span> mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.44.0-jammy /bin/sh <span class="nt">-c</span> <span class="s2">"cd /home/pwuser &amp;&amp; npx -y playwright@1.44.0 run-server --port 8080"</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="alert alert-warning">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Unsafe Environment</h4>
Keep in mind this is just for development purposes inside your local system and don’t try to expose your container network to the host system using --network host on production or CI
</div>

<p>In the last step go to ui folder,</p>
<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nb">cd </span>ui<span class="p">;</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="run-the-test-cases-with-playwright-cli">Run the test cases with Playwright CLI</h2>

<p>There are several options we can use to run the test cases, in CLI:</p>

<p>To run playwright UI mode using the browser, you can add <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">--ui</code> in the cli, for example:</p>
<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>npx playwright <span class="nb">test</span> <span class="nt">--ui</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>If you are using playwright from docker, you can use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">--ui-port=&lt;playwright-docker-server&gt;</code>, for example:</p>
<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>npx playwright <span class="nb">test</span> <span class="nt">--ui-port</span><span class="o">=</span>8080
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>To run playwright for specific project only, for example meshery-provider, you can run this command:</p>
<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>npx playwright <span class="nb">test</span> <span class="nt">--ui</span> <span class="nt">--project</span><span class="o">=</span>chromium-meshery-provider 
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>To run specific test, you can add the test file location, for example:</p>
<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>npx playwright <span class="nb">test</span> <span class="nt">--ui</span> <span class="nt">--project</span><span class="o">=</span>chromium-meshery-provider tests/e2e/service-mesh-performance.spec.js 
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>For more detail, you can read the <a href="https://playwright.dev/docs/test-cli">Playwright Cli docs</a></p>

<h2 id="testing-meshery--local-provider">Testing Meshery &amp; Local Provider</h2>

<p>By default our test cases is running against both Meshery and Local Provider, we are utilizing playwright feature such as:</p>

<ul>
  <li>StorageState: In meshery <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/ui/tests/e2e/auth.setup.js">setup auth</a>, we have 2 storage state, which store a session for Meshery and Local provider.</li>
  <li>Project: After the setup completes, it will run the project-based test depending on which storage state for the Local Provider and one for the Meshery Provider</li>
  <li>Test Parameterize:  In the Local provider we are limiting some features to test against. For the missing features, we leverage this playwright feature to check or even skip the test. If it is not possible to run then you need to specify the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">provider</code> directly from the test, and make sure the test is wrapped using:</li>
</ul>

<div class="language-javascript highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">import</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nx">expect</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nx">test</span> <span class="p">}</span> <span class="k">from</span> <span class="dl">'</span><span class="s1">./fixtures/project</span><span class="dl">'</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="nx">test</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="dl">'</span><span class="s1">Random test</span><span class="dl">'</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">async</span> <span class="p">({</span> <span class="nx">provider</span> <span class="p">})</span> <span class="o">=&gt;</span> <span class="p">{</span>
  <span class="k">if</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="nx">provider</span> <span class="o">===</span> <span class="dl">"</span><span class="s2">Meshery</span><span class="dl">"</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="c1">// Run this for testing Meshery provider</span>
  <span class="p">}</span>

  <span class="k">if</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="nx">provider</span> <span class="o">===</span> <span class="dl">"</span><span class="s2">None</span><span class="dl">"</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="c1">// Run this for testing Local provider</span>
  <span class="p">}</span>
<span class="p">});</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="testing-policy">Testing Policy</h2>

<p>After merging a pull request, ensuring test stability across CI/CD runs is crucial. A test may pass locally but fail in the CI/CD environment due to differences in execution conditions. While one approach is to mark all new tests as @unstable by default, a more effective strategy is to apply the @unstable tag only if a test exhibits intermittent failures or flaky behavior.</p>

<p>After merging into the master branch, monitor the GitHub workflow that executes the new test case and assess its stability. If the test fails, raise another PR to mark it as @unstable and communicate this to the team. For example:</p>

<div class="language-javascript highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">import</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nx">expect</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nx">test</span> <span class="p">}</span> <span class="k">from</span> <span class="dl">'</span><span class="s1">./fixtures/project</span><span class="dl">'</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="nx">test</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="dl">'</span><span class="s1">Random test</span><span class="dl">'</span><span class="p">,</span>  <span class="p">{</span> <span class="na">tag</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="dl">'</span><span class="s1">@unstable</span><span class="dl">'</span> <span class="p">},</span> <span class="k">async</span> <span class="p">({</span> <span class="nx">provider</span> <span class="p">})</span> <span class="o">=&gt;</span> <span class="p">{</span>
  <span class="c1">// Test cases here</span>
  <span class="c1">// ...</span>
<span class="p">});</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="debugging-test-on-github-actions">Debugging Test on Github Actions</h2>

<p>End-to-end test results are stored as artifacts on every PR in Github Actions. In case you need to debug a failed test:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Visit the PR in question. Go to the bottom of PR directly above the comment.</li>
  <li>Wait until all Github Actions completed, and scroll until you see <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Meshery UI and Server / UI end-to-end tests</code></li>
  <li>Click details and it will redirect you to the actions workflow</li>
  <li>Go to summary tab, scroll down until you see artifact, and check the artifact <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">playwright-report</code></li>
  <li>Download the artifact</li>
  <li>Extract the file into a folder</li>
  <li>Go to <a href="https://trace.playwright.dev/">Playwright Trace Page</a></li>
  <li>From the test folder pick one folder which represents the test, you want to check</li>
  <li>Upload the trace file</li>
</ul>

<p>Watch the training session on Playwright testing and trace debugging.</p>

<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/x-W60mvDYuo?si=coN7RpRjkI4a_ndk&amp;start=1524" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen=""></iframe>

<h3 id="find-tests-here">Find Tests here</h3>
<p>Refer to <a href="https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/13Ir4gfaKoAX9r8qYjAFFl_U9ntke4X5ndREY1T7bnVs/edit?usp=sharing">Meshery Test Plan</a> for test scenarios.</p>

<p>To filter and view only UI-related tests using the Sheet Views feature:</p>
<ol>
  <li>In the top menu bar, click Data → Change view</li>
  <li>Choose the pre-defined view labeled “UI”</li>
</ol>

<p><img src="/v0.8/assets/img/contributing/meshery-test-plan-v0.8.0-ui.png" alt="Meshery Test Plan Screenshot" /></p>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

<!-- <a href="http://idratherbewriting.com" class="noCrossRef productSubtitle"> Home </a> > <a class="noCrossRef productSubtitle" href="https://docs.meshery.io">Learn API Doc</a> > contributing-ui-widgets -->

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Contributing to Meshery UI - Dashboard Widgets</h1>
           <div class="prereqs"><p><strong style="font-size: 20px;">Prerequisite Reading</strong></p>
  <ol><li><a href="contributing-ui">Contributing to Meshery UI</a></li></ol>
</div>

<p>Meshery’s dashboard is a composable and extensible interface made up of individual widgets. These widgets allow contributors to surface specific Meshery data or capabilities within a modular layout system.</p>

<p>This guide walks through the process of creating and integrating a custom widget into the <a href="https://playground.meshery.io/">Meshery dashboard</a>. You’ll learn about layout configuration, design best practices, and how to register new widgets.</p>

<h2 id="1-widget-architecture">1. Widget Architecture</h2>

<p>Widgets are React components located <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/tree/master/ui/components/DashboardComponent/widgets">here</a>:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>/ui/components/DashboardComponent/widgets/
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Each widget is rendered inside a card component (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">&lt;PlainCard /&gt;</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">&lt;DesignCard /&gt;</code>, etc.), which is sourced from the <a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sistent/sistent">Sistent design system</a>.</p>

<p>Widgets can:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Pull data from APIs (REST, GraphQL, RSS)</li>
  <li>Display static links or interactive components</li>
  <li>Include icons and thumbnails for user familiarity</li>
</ul>

<hr />

<h2 id="2-creating-a-new-widget">2. Creating a New Widget</h2>

<p>Create a new file inside <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">widgets/</code>, e.g.:</p>

<div class="language-jsx highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="sr">/ui/</span><span class="nx">components</span><span class="o">/</span><span class="nx">DashboardComponent</span><span class="o">/</span><span class="nx">widgets</span><span class="o">/</span><span class="nx">LatestBlogs</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">js</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Use design system components from <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@sistent/sistent</code>:</p>

<div class="language-jsx highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">import</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nx">useTheme</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nx">PlainCard</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nx">BellIcon</span> <span class="p">}</span> <span class="k">from</span> <span class="dl">"</span><span class="s2">@sistent/sistent</span><span class="dl">"</span><span class="p">;</span>

<span class="kd">const</span> <span class="nx">LatestBlogs</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="nx">props</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">=&gt;</span> <span class="p">{</span>
  <span class="kd">const</span> <span class="nx">theme</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nx">useTheme</span><span class="p">();</span>
  <span class="kd">const</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="na">data</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nx">blogs</span> <span class="p">}</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nx">useFetchBlogsQuery</span><span class="p">();</span> <span class="c1">// fetch data from rtk query</span>

  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="p">(</span>
    <span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">PlainCard</span>
      <span class="na">title</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="s">"LATEST BLOGS"</span>
      <span class="na">icon</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="si">{</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">BellIcon</span> <span class="si">{</span><span class="p">...</span><span class="nx">props</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">iconsProps</span><span class="si">}</span> <span class="p">/&gt;</span><span class="si">}</span>
      <span class="na">resources</span><span class="p">=</span><span class="si">{</span><span class="nx">resources</span><span class="si">}</span>
    <span class="p">/&gt;</span>
  <span class="p">);</span>
<span class="p">};</span>

<span class="k">export</span> <span class="k">default</span> <span class="nx">LatestBlogs</span><span class="p">;</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">useTheme()</code> for consistent color tokens across themes.</p>

<hr />

<h2 id="3-adding-thumbnails">3. Adding Thumbnails</h2>

<p>Thumbnails are image previews of widgets. Place them here:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>/ui/components/DashboardComponent/widgets/Thumbnails/
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Recommended format: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.png</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.svg</code></p>

<p>Example:</p>

<div class="language-js highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">import</span> <span class="nx">LatestBlogsThumbnail</span> <span class="k">from</span> <span class="dl">"</span><span class="s2">./Thumbnails/LatestBlogs.png</span><span class="dl">"</span><span class="p">;</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>To verify your thumbnail appears correctly, click on the “Edit” button on the Dashboard. A visual card with your thumbnail and widget title will be listed there, allowing users to add it to their layout.</p>

<hr />

<h2 id="4-registering-the-widget">4. Registering the Widget</h2>

<p>Register your widget inside <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">getWidgets.js</code>:</p>

<div class="language-jsx highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">export</span> <span class="kd">const</span> <span class="nx">getWidgets</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">()</span> <span class="o">=&gt;</span> <span class="p">({</span>
  <span class="na">LATEST_BLOGS</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">{</span>
    <span class="na">title</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="dl">"</span><span class="s2">Latest Blogs</span><span class="dl">"</span><span class="p">,</span>
    <span class="na">isEnabled</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nx">alwaysShown</span><span class="p">,</span>
    <span class="na">component</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">LatestBlogs</span> <span class="p">/&gt;,</span>
    <span class="na">defaultSizing</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="na">w</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="na">h</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="mi">2</span> <span class="p">},</span>
    <span class="na">thumbnail</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nx">LatestBlogsThumbnail</span><span class="p">?.</span><span class="nx">src</span><span class="p">,</span>
  <span class="p">},</span>
<span class="p">});</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<ul>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">title</code>: Display name</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">component</code>: JSX element</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">isEnabled</code>: Visibility flag</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">defaultSizing</code>: Default dimensions</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">thumbnail</code>: Path to preview image</li>
</ul>

<hr />

<h2 id="5-adding-to-default-layout">5. Adding to Default Layout</h2>

<p>To include your widget in the default dashboard layout:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>/ui/components/DashboardComponent/defaultLayout.js
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Layouts are defined per <strong>screen size breakpoint</strong> (e.g., <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">sm</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">xs</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">xxs</code>) to ensure responsiveness. Each layout item is an object with grid-based properties defined by the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">react-grid-layout</code> library.</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>sm: tablets and desktops
xs: large phones
xxs: small phones
</code></pre></div></div>

<h3 id="example-layout-item">Example Layout Item:</h3>

<div class="language-js highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="p">{</span>
  <span class="nl">h</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">,</span>                  <span class="c1">// Height in grid units</span>
  <span class="nx">i</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="dl">'</span><span class="s1">LATEST_BLOGS</span><span class="dl">'</span><span class="p">,</span>     <span class="c1">// Widget identifier (unique string)</span>
  <span class="nx">moved</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">,</span>          <span class="c1">// Internal flag (do not change manually)</span>
  <span class="kd">static</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">,</span>         <span class="c1">// If true, the widget cannot be dragged or resized</span>
  <span class="nx">w</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">,</span>                  <span class="c1">// Width in grid units</span>
  <span class="nx">x</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span>                  <span class="c1">// Horizontal grid position (column index)</span>
  <span class="nx">y</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span>                  <span class="c1">// Vertical grid position (row index)</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h3 id="layout-field-descriptions">Layout Field Descriptions:</h3>

<ul>
  <li><strong>i</strong>: A unique string ID for the widget. This should match the widget’s <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">id</code> used elsewhere in your code.</li>
  <li><strong>x</strong>: The column (starting from 0) where the widget should be placed.</li>
  <li><strong>y</strong>: The row (starting from 0) where the widget should be placed. Widgets with the same <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">y</code> value appear in the same row.</li>
  <li><strong>w</strong>: The widget’s width in terms of number of grid columns it should span.</li>
  <li><strong>h</strong>: The widget’s height in terms of number of grid rows it should span.</li>
  <li><strong>static</strong>: When <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">true</code>, the widget is locked in place — it can’t be moved or resized.</li>
  <li><strong>moved</strong>: Used by the library to track user interactions. Leave as <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">false</code>.</li>
</ul>

<blockquote>
  <p>Here layout is based on a 12-column CSS grid. Each widget’s position is defined in terms of this virtual grid, which helps in building a responsive and flexible dashboard layout.</p>
</blockquote>

<hr />

<p>Define the widget’s position (x, y) and size (w, h) in each breakpoint for responsive behavior. The code for it can be found <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/ui/components/DashboardComponent/defaultLayout.js">here</a>.</p>

<p>Note: Layouts for <strong>Remote Providers</strong> are dynamically generated based on user configuration and stored remotely. Local providers use a predefined layout (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">LOCAL_PROVIDER_LAYOUT</code>). Widgets must be added to both if you want consistent behavior across environments.</p>

<p>Meshery stores user layout preferences either in local storage or via the provider’s backend, depending on login state.</p>

<p>This is how your default widget would appear in the dashboard:</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/dashboard-widget/dashboard-widgets.png">
<img style="width: 600px;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/dashboard-widget/dashboard-widgets.png" />
</a></p>

<hr />

<h2 id="6-best-practices">6. Best Practices</h2>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Naming</strong>: Use uppercase keys (e.g. <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">MY_DESIGNS</code>) for clarity</li>
  <li><strong>Icons</strong>: Use consistent design system icons (e.g., <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">CatalogIcon</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">DesignIcon</code>)</li>
  <li><strong>Themes</strong>: Use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">useTheme()</code> to access tokens</li>
  <li><strong>Responsiveness</strong>: Define layout for multiple viewports (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">sm</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">xs</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">xxs</code>)</li>
  <li><strong>Reusability</strong>: Break logic into reusable hooks when needed</li>
  <li><strong>Thumbnails</strong>: Always include a visual thumbnail</li>
  <li><strong>Permissions</strong>: If your widget accesses protected resources, ensure user has correct provider login state or roles.</li>
</ul>

<hr />

<hr />

<h2 id="8-publishing">8. Publishing</h2>

<p>Once your widget is working:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Ensure it appears in the widget selector UI</li>
  <li>Validate layout and responsiveness</li>
  <li>Submit a PR with the new component, layout entry, and thumbnail. <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/pull/13629">Here</a> is a PR that adds Latest Blogs widget to Meshery Dashboard.</li>
  <li>Add your widget in the <a href="https://meshery.io/extensions">Meshery Extensions Catalog</a> if appropriate</li>
</ul>

</script>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

          <h1>Contributing to Meshery UI</h1>
           <h2 id="ui-contribution-flow"><a name="contributing-ui">UI Contribution Flow</a></h2>

<p>Meshery UI is built on React and Next.js. In nearly all cases, while contributing to Meshery UI, you will need to build and run Meshery Server as well. Meshery Server is written in <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Go</code> (Golang) and leverages Go Modules. To make building of each component easier a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Makefile</code> is included in the main repository folder. Use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">make</code> to build any and all components.</p>

<h2 id="architecture">Architecture</h2>

<p>The following is a list of top-level frameworks, libraries, design system used in Meshery UI.</p>

<ul>
  <li><a href="https://nextjs.org/">NextJS</a> - Server and router</li>
  <li><a href="https://reactjs.org/">ReactJS</a> - User Interface library</li>
  <li><a href="https://material-ui.com/">Material UI</a> - Design System</li>
  <li><a href="https://naver.github.io/billboard.js/">BillboardJS</a> - Charting library, used for exposing Grafana and Prometheus-collected metrics</li>
  <li><a href="https://js.cytoscape.org/">CytoscapeJS</a> - a visualization tool for canvas-based, visual topology (networks)</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="build-system">Build System</h3>

<p>Meshery UI and Provider UI use <a href="https://nextjs.org/">Next.js</a> with <a href="https://swc.rs/">SWC</a> (Speedy Web Compiler) for fast builds and optimal performance.</p>

<h2 id="schema-driven-ui-development">Schema-Driven UI Development</h2>

<p>Meshery UI uses a schema-driven approach where components and forms are generated from JSON schemas. This enables dynamic UI adaptation, consistent validation, and type-safety across the application.</p>

<p><strong>⚠️ Required Reading:</strong> Before contributing, you must read the <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/project/contributing/contributing-ui-schemas">Schema-Driven UI Development Guide</a> to understand how Meshery’s UI components are generated and maintained using schemas.</p>

<h2 id="meshery-server-apis">Meshery Server APIs</h2>

<p>The <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/extensibility/api">API overview</a> in the Extensibility guide offers high-level insight, while each API reference (below) offers details pertaining to each API endpoints’ behavior and use.</p>

<h3 id="rest-api">REST API</h3>

<p>Meshery provides a REST API available through the default port of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">9081/tcp</code> at <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">&lt;hostname&gt;:&lt;port&gt;/api/</code>. See the <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/reference/rest-apis">REST API Reference</a> for a complete list of endpoints available with short description of their purpose and example code.</p>

<h3 id="graphql-api">GraphQL API</h3>

<p>Meshery provides a GraphQl API available through the default port of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">9081/tcp</code> at <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">&lt;hostname&gt;:&lt;port&gt;/api/graphql/query</code>. See the <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/reference/graphql-apis">GraphQL API Reference</a> <a href="https://relay.dev">Relay</a> is the client used.</p>

<h2 id="design">Design</h2>

<p>Meshery UI is a significant component of the value proposition Meshery offers to individuals and organizations seeking to adopt and operate a cloud native infrastructure.</p>

<h3 id="user-flows--wireframing--mockups">User Flows / Wireframing / Mockups</h3>

<p>Figma is used as the user flow and UI mockup design tool. The <a href="https://www.figma.com/file/SMP3zxOjZztdOLtgN4dS2W/Meshery-UI">Meshery UI design file</a> can be viewed by using this <a href="https://www.figma.com/team_invite/redeem/GvB8SudhEOoq3JOvoLaoMs">open invitation</a> for view access. Fill-in a <a href="https://meshery.io/newcomers">community member form</a> to gain access to additional community resources.</p>

<h3 id="design-goals">Design Goals</h3>

<p>The designs in this specification should result in enabling:</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p><strong>User experience should be intuitive</strong> - Meshery’s UX, which includes Meshery UI as a component of the overall UX, needs to be simple, but powerful. This is achieved through intuitive layouts and predefined filters that accommodate common tasks. This is achieved through sensible defaults, consistency of user interaction paradigms and features that delight the user.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Extensible</strong> - Meshery UI should be a first-class component of Meshery, but also facilitate third-party integrations.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><strong>Real-time</strong> - Meshery UI should be event-driven where possible.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<h2 id="setup">Setup</h2>

<div class="alert alert-info">
<h4 class="alert-heading">Windows User?</h4>
See <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/project/contributing/meshery-windows">Setting up Meshery Development Environment on Windows</a>.
</div>

<h3 id="required-node-version">Required Node Version</h3>

<p>Node 20 LTS</p>

<h3 id="linting-ui">Linting-UI</h3>

<p>When contributing to Meshery UI, it is advisable to:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Use prettier plugin for Visual Studio Code.</li>
  <li>Disable plugins other than <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">prettier</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">eslint</code> for formatting and linting, if any.</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="install-ui-dependencies">Install UI dependencies</h3>

<p>To install/update the UI dependencies:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">make ui-setup</code>
</div>
</pre>

<h3 id="build-and-export-ui">Build and export UI</h3>

<p>To build and export the UI code:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">make ui-build</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>Using this command, changes that you make are not rebuilt automatically. You will have to run this command again to rebuild the UI and see them.</p>

<p>Now that the UI code is built, Meshery UI will be available at <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">http://localhost:9081</code> when Meshery Server is running (Read below).</p>

<p>To build and export the UI code <em>and</em> build and run Meshery Server:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">make ui-server</code>
</div>
</pre>

<h2 id="run-meshery-server">Run Meshery Server</h2>

<p>To start running Meshery Server locally:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">make server</code>
</div>
</pre>
<p>Now, Meshery will run on the default port <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">http://localhost:9081</code>.</p>

<p><strong>Please note</strong>: If you see “Meshery Development Incompatible” while trying to sign into Meshery Server, then follow these steps:</p>

<p><a href="/v0.8/assets/img/meshery-development-incompatible-error.png">
  <img style="width: 600px;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/meshery-development-incompatible-error.png" />
</a></p>

<p>Potential Solution:</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p>Go to your meshery folder in your local-system where you’ve cloned it.
Execute:</p>
  </li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">git remote add upstream https://github.com/meshery/meshery</code></li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">git fetch upstream</code></li>
  <li>Restart the meshery server</li>
  <li>Additionally, before restarting the server, if you like to pull the latest changes, you can do: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">git pull upstream master</code></li>
</ul>

<h3 id="ui-development-server">UI Development Server</h3>

<p>If you want to work on the UI, it will be a good idea to use the included UI development server. You can run the UI development server by running the following command:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">make ui</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>Refer to <a href="contributing-server">Contributing to Meshery Server</a>, if needed.</p>

<blockquote>
  <p>Make sure to have Meshery Server configured, up and running on the default port <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">http://localhost:9081</code> and choose a provider to login with (visit <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">http://localhost:9081</code>) before proceeding to access and work on the UI server at <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">http://localhost:3000</code>.</p>
</blockquote>

<p>Any UI changes made now will <em>automatically</em> be rebuilt and served in your browser.</p>

<h3 id="running-end-to-end-integration-tests">Running end-to-end integration tests</h3>

<p>Refer to <a href="contributing-ui-tests">Meshery UI Testing</a> for details of how to contribute and benefit from Meshery UI testing.</p>

<h3 id="static-files-icons-and-images">Static Files, Icons and Images</h3>

<p>The Meshery UI public folder contains static files. Its folder structure looks like this:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>meshery
└── ui
    └── public
        └── static
            ├── favicon.png
            ├── fonts
            ├── img
            └── style
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Images and icons used in Meshery UI need to be sourced from the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/tree/master/ui/public/static/img">public directory of images</a>. The files written inside this directory should only end with the extensions like <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.svg</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.png</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.jpg</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.jpeg</code>. Always use vector-based graphics (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.svg</code>), unless your have extenuating circumstances.</p>

<h5 id="conventions-for-svg-files">Conventions for SVG files</h5>

<ol>
  <li>SVGs should be optimized and compressed.
    <ol>
      <li>Use an online, SVG optimizer, like https://www.svgviewer.dev, to compress the file(s) to smaller size.</li>
    </ol>
  </li>
  <li>All SVGs should have <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">height</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">width</code> properties set to 20px x 20px by default. Ensure that height and width attributes are always set in original SVG.</li>
  <li>All SVGs should have <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">height</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">width</code> included as a style prop in their React component.</li>
  <li>Always include this XML header in each SVG image:</li>
</ol>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">&lt;?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?&gt;&lt;!DOCTYPE svg&gt;</div></div>
</pre>
<ol>
  <li>Svg can only fall under two categories, and this categories should be the name of folder 
    <ol>
      <li>white: containing white or mono-colored version of that SVG</li>
      <li>color: containing colored version of that SVG.
e.g.: the Meshery logo icon folder structure looks like this:
        <div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>└── img
 └── meshery
     ├── white
     |   └── meshery-white.svg
     └── color
         └── meshery-color.svg
</code></pre></div>        </div>
      </li>
    </ol>
  </li>
  <li>Avoid any kind of duplicity in the versions of icons used.</li>
</ol>

<p>For accessing the svg file as data-url, the utf8 encoding should be used in place of base64.Use <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/encodeURIComponent">encodeURIComponent</a> on SVG data URIs. \</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">let svg = &#39;data:image/svg+xml;utf8,&#39; + encodeURIComponent(svgFile);</code>
</div>
</pre>

                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });

           <h1 id="contributing">Contributing</h1>

<p>Please do! Thanks for your help! 🎈 Meshery is community-built and welcomes collaboration. Contributors are expected to adhere to the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md">CNCF’s Code of Conduct</a>.</p>

<h2 id="general-contribution-flow">General Contribution Flow</h2>

<p>Meshery and it’s various architectural components are written in different languages, including Golang, Javascript (React.js and Next.js) To make building, testing, and the experience of contributing consistent across all Meshery components, a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Makefile</code> is included in the every repository. These <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">make</code> targets are what you will use to build, run, test, and document.</p>

<p>To contribute to Meshery, please follow this basic fork-and-pull request <a href="/v0.8/project/contributing/contributing-gitflow">gitflow</a>.</p>

<details>
<summary>Adding your sign-off on commits (Developer Certificate of Origin)</summary>
<ul>
<li>
To contribute to this project, you must agree to the Developer Certificate of
Origin (DCO) for each commit you make. The DCO is a simple statement that you,
as a contributor, have the legal right to make the contribution.
</li>

<li>
See the <a href="https://developercertificate.org"> DCO </a> file for the full text of what you must agree to
and how it works <a href="https://github.com/probot/dco#how-it-works">here</a>.
To signify that you agree to the DCO for contributions, you simply add a line to each of your
git commit messages:

<pre><code>
Signed-off-by: Jane Smith &lt;jane.smith@example.com&gt;
</code></pre></li>

<li>
In most cases, you can add this signoff to your commit automatically with the
<code>-s</code> or <code>--signoff</code> flag to <code>git commit</code>. You must use your real name and a reachable email
address (sorry, no pseudonyms or anonymous contributions). An example of signing off on a commit:

<pre><code>$ git commit -s -m “my commit message w/signoff”</code></pre>
</li>

<li>
To ensure all your commits are signed, you may choose to add this alias to your global <code>.gitconfig</code>:

~/.gitconfig

<pre><code>
[alias]
  amend = commit -s --amend
  cm = commit -s -m
  commit = commit -s
</code></pre>

Or you may configure your IDE, for example, VSCode to automatically sign-off commits for you:<a href="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7570704/64490167-98906400-d25a-11e9-8b8a-5f465b854d49.png"><img src="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7570704/64490167-98906400-d25a-11e9-8b8a-5f465b854d49.png" width="50%" /></a>

</li>
</ul>
</details>

<h2 id="not-sure-where-to-start">Not sure where to start?</h2>

<details>
<summary>Follow these steps and you'll be right at home.</summary>
<ol>
  <li>See the <a href="https://meshery.io/community">Newcomers Guide</a> for how, where, and why to contribute.</li>
  <li>Sign up for a <a href="https://meshery.io/community#meshmates"><em>MeshMate</em></a> to find the perfect Mentor to help you explore the projects and find your place in the community.</li>
  <li><strong>Familiarize</strong> yourself with the broader set of projects in Meshery's ecosystem, including the <a href="https://github.com/meshery-extensions">meshery-extensions</a>. Spend time understanding each of the initiatives through high-level overviews available in the community drive and through discussions with your MeshMate.</li>
  <li><strong>Identify</strong> your area of interest: Use the time with your MeshMate to familiarize yourself with the architecture and technologies used in the projects. Inform your MeshMate of your current skills and what skills you aim to develop.</li>
  <li><strong><a href="https://play.meshery.io">Play with Meshery</a></strong>: Put on your user hat and walk-through all of Meshery’s features and functions as a user.</li>
  <li><strong>Build Meshery Server and UI</strong>: Confirm that you have a usable development environment. See <a href="#contributing-guides">Guides</a> below.</li>
  <li><strong>Discuss</strong> with the community by engaging in the <a href="https://discuss.meshery.io">discussion forum</a>.</li>
  <li><strong>Contribute</strong> by grabbing any open issue with the <a href="https://github.com/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+archived%3Afalse+org%3Ameshery+org%3Ameshery-extensions+org%3Aservice-mesh-performance+org%3Aservice-mesh-patterns+label%3A%22help+wanted%22+">help-wanted label</a> and jump in. If needed, create a <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/issues/new/choose">new issue</a>. All <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/pulls">pull requests</a> should reference an open issue. Include keywords in your pull request descriptions, as well as commit messages, to <a href="https://help.github.com/en/github/managing-your-work-on-github/closing-issues-using-keywords">automatically close issues in GitHub</a>.</li>
  <li><strong>Fill in</strong> a <a href="https://meshery.io/newcomers">community member form</a> to gain access to community resources.</li>
</ol>
</details>

<script>
$(document).ready(function() {

    var toc = $('#TOC');

    // Select each header
    sections = $('.td-content h1');
        $.each(sections, function(idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if(!section.hasClass('noTOC')){
               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>

<!-- <a href="http://idratherbewriting.com" class="noCrossRef productSubtitle"> Home </a> > <a class="noCrossRef productSubtitle" href="https://docs.meshery.io">Learn API Doc</a> > meshery-windows -->

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Setting up Meshery Development Environment on Windows</h1>
           <p>You can use one of the following three approaches to setup a Meshery development environment in Windows:</p>
<ol>
  <li>Using WSL or WSL2 (Recommended)</li>
  <li>Natively (directly) on Windows</li>
  <li>Using Hyper-V to create a Linux VM</li>
</ol>

<p>Setting up a Meshery development environment on WSL(2) or Hyper-V is not much different from setting up on a native Linux platform. The same instructions can be followed as already documented.</p>

<p>All three methods require the same prerequisites mentioned below in the <a href="#prerequisites">Prerequisites</a> section but the Linux-based methods/platforms come with some of the prerequisites pre-installed and have no issues with Linux style commands making it easier to setup the environment.</p>

<p>Additionally, all three require methods will require access to a Kubernetes cluster which can be a kind, minikube, Kubernetes in Docker or a cluster elsewhere with network access.</p>

<h2 id="prerequisites">Prerequisites</h2>

<p>All three methods require the following prerequisites:</p>
<ul>
  <li>make</li>
  <li>gcc</li>
  <li>nodejs (for npm)</li>
  <li>go</li>
  <li>Git or Git Bash</li>
  <li>Visual Studio Code for development</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="compatibility">Compatibility</h2>

<p>The following minimum Windows build versions are required:</p>
<table id="compatibility-table">
  <tr>
    <th id="model">Name</th>
    <th id="model">Version</th> 
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><a href="#wsl1">WSL1</a></td>
    <td><b>x64</b> - Windows 7 </td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><a href="#wsl2">WSL2</a></td>
    <td><b>x64</b> - Version 1903, Build 18362; <b>ARM 64</b> - Version 2004, Build 19041</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><a href="https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/release-notes#build-18945">Custom Kernel</a></td>
    <td>Build 18945</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><a href="https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/release-notes#build-19013">Kernel with K8s required modules</a></td>
    <td>Build 19013</td>
  </tr>
</table>

<p>Note
<br />Run the following command on Powershell to check your Windows build and version:</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">[System.Environment]::OSVersion.Version</div></div>
 </pre>

<h2 id="using-wsl2">Using WSL2</h2>

<p>Here is a link to setting up WSL2: <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install">https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install</a></p>

<p>Once WSL is setup, login to the WSL distribution and use the steps for Linux to setup the development environment.</p>

<h3 id="steps">Steps</h3>
<p>Perform the following steps in order:</p>

<h4 id="1-enable-and-configure-windows-subsystem-for-linux-wsl">1. Enable and configure Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL)</h4>

<p>Open Powershell in administrator mode and run:</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">dism.exe /online /enable-feature /featurename:Microsoft-Windows-Subsystem-Linux /all /norestart

Restart-Computer</div></div>
</pre>

<p>For more information visit <a href="https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install-win10">How to install Linux on Windows with WSL</a>.</p>

<h4 id="2-configuring-wsl">2. Configuring WSL</h4>

<p>Enable VM (Virtual Machine) feature. To do so open <em>PowerShell</em> in administrator mode and run:</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">dism.exe /online /enable-feature /featurename:VirtualMachinePlatform /all /norestart</div></div>
</pre>

<p>Ensure WSL2 is the default version:</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">wsl --set-default-version 2</div></div>
</pre>

<h4 id="3-install-a-new-distro">3. Install a new distro</h4>

<p>Refer to the instructions <a href="https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install-win10#install-your-linux-distribution-of-choice">here</a> to install a new distro such as Ubuntu by default.
Feel free to use any distro of your choice.</p>

<h4 id="4-enable-docker">4. Enable Docker</h4>

<p>The Docker Desktop application for Windows includes a comprehensive set of tools, including Docker Engine, Docker CLI client, Docker Compose, Notary, Kubernetes, and a Credential Helper.</p>

<table id="compatibility-table">
  <tr>
    <th id="model">Windows 10 Version</th>
    <th id="model">Docker Desktop</th> 
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>Pro/Education/Enterprise</td>
    <td><a href="https://docs.docker.com/docker-for-windows/install/">Docker Desktop for Windows Pro</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>Home</td>
    <td><a href="https://docs.docker.com/docker-for-windows/install-windows-home/">Docker Desktop for Windows Home</a></td>
  </tr>
</table>

<h2 id="natively-on-windows">Natively on Windows</h2>

<p>This approach can be the most challenging to setup among all and is recommended for users that are very conversant with setting up development environments in Windows.
make, gcc and the other prerequisites do not come pre-installed on Windows and hence these need to be installed manually. You will also need to set the <strong>Path</strong> in <em>Environment Variables</em> for some of them like <em>make</em> and <em>gcc</em>.</p>

<h3 id="installing-prerequsites">Installing prerequsites:</h3>
<p>Here are some links and recommendations to install the prerequisites:</p>

<h4 id="--make">- make</h4>

<p>Use the <a href="https://gnuwin32.sourceforge.net/downlinks/make.php">setup program</a> to download the installation package and run it to install make and other dependencies.</p>

<p>If the download link fails, visit the home page at <a href="https://gnuwin32.sourceforge.net/packages/make.htm">https://gnuwin32.sourceforge.net/packages/make.htm</a></p>

<h4 id="--gcc">- gcc</h4>

<p>Use the <a href="https://www.mingw-w64.org/">mingw-w64</a> project for gcc. The pre-built binaries can be downloaded from <a href="https://github.com/niXman/mingw-builds-binaries/releases">https://github.com/niXman/mingw-builds-binaries/releases</a>. For a typical 64-bit Windows, it is of the **x86<em>64-XX.X.X-release-posix-seh-ucrt-XX_XXX-XXXX.7z** format. Posix provides cross-platform compatibility and is known to work well. After extracting and copying (typically to the C:\ drive at root), add the path to the <strong>Path</strong> variable in _Environment Variables</em>.</p>

<p>For example, here’s a <a href="https://github.com/niXman/mingw-builds-binaries/releases/download/15.2.0-rt_v13-rev0/x86_64-15.2.0-release-posix-seh-ucrt-rt_v13-rev0.7z">direct download link</a> to the latest release as of this writing. After installing, ensure the path is in the <strong>Path</strong> variable in <em>Environment Variables</em>. It is usually added automatically.</p>

<p>The <em>Cygwin</em> project is known to fail with errors.</p>

<p>For more information, visit <a href="https://gcc.gnu.org/install/binaries.html">https://gcc.gnu.org/install/binaries.html</a></p>

<h4 id="--nodejs-for-npm">- nodejs (for npm)</h4>

<p>You will need <strong>Node 20</strong>. Download it from <a href="https://nodejs.org/en/download">https://nodejs.org/en/download</a> and install it. The path is usually automatically added.</p>

<h4 id="--go">- go</h4>

<p>Visit <a href="https://go.dev/doc/install">https://go.dev/doc/install</a> to download and install Go. Please use the version specified in the project’s <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">go.mod</code> file. As of this writing, Meshery uses <strong>1.26.4</strong>. The path is usually automatically added.</p>

<h4 id="--git-bash">- Git Bash</h4>

<p>Git Bash is a terminal emulator which provides git and Linux-like command line experience. You can download it from: https://git-scm.com/downloads.</p>

<h3 id="verify-prerequisites">Verify prerequisites</h3>

<p>Launch Git Bash, PowerShell or VS Code Terminal and run the following commands to ensure prerequisites are met:</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">make --version</div></div>
</pre>

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">gcc --version</div></div>
</pre>

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">node --version</div></div>
</pre>

<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">go version</div></div>
</pre>

<p>If any of these result in command not found error, check if the PATH in environment variables has been set properly. To launch the environment variables window Here’s an example:
<a href="/v0.8/assets/img/contributing/win-environment-variables.png">
  <img style="max-width: 450px;" src="/v0.8/assets/img/contributing/win-environment-variables.png" />
</a></p>

<p>You are now ready to <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/project/contributing/">contribute</a> to Meshery.</p>

<h2 id="using-hyper-v-to-install-a-linux-vm">Using Hyper-V to install a linux VM</h2>

<p>Here is a link to install linux VM using Hyper-V: <a href="https://wiki.ubuntu.com/Hyper-V">https://wiki.ubuntu.com/Hyper-V</a></p>

<h2 id="get-the-code">Get the code</h2>

<ul>
  <li>Fork and then clone the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery">Meshery repository</a>
    <div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nv">$ </span>git clone https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/meshery
</code></pre></div>    </div>
  </li>
</ul>

               var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
              var parent = $("#" + div_id)
              var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text +'">' + div_text +'</a></li>';
              $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            // Add section code to subnavigation
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil("h1");
            $.each(contenders, function(idx, contender){
               if( !$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && ($(contender).is('h2') || $(contender).is('h3')) ) {
                   var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                   var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                   var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text +'">' + contender_text +'</a></li>';
                   children.append(content);
                }
             })
             $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        //added 'selected' tag to the first element of toc
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function(e){
          // Detect how far are we from the top of the page
          let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
          // Loop through every navigation menu item
          $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {       
              if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
              // Remove 'selected' from previously highlighted menu items
              $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              // Highlight the current menu item by adding 'selected' class
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
          if($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
            $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
              $(this).addClass('selected');
          }
        });
      })
      // Smooth scroll to target section when clicking on TOC link
      $('a[href^="#"]').on('click', function(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        var target = $(this.hash);
        if (target.length) {
          $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 115
          }, 1000);
        }
      });
    });
</script>
